items.stem: Which of the following best describes the purpose of corporate governance in a company?

options.text: To direct and control the company in the interests of its stakeholders and ensure accountability
options.rationale: Correct: governance is the system by which companies are directed and controlled, promoting accountability.

options.text: To maximise short-term share price at any cost
options.rationale: Governance is broader than short-term price and includes accountability and ethics.

options.text: To prepare the company's tax return
options.rationale: Tax compliance is a specific task, not the purpose of governance.

options.text: To set the daily production schedule
options.rationale: Operational scheduling is a management task, not governance.

items.explanation: Correct: governance is the system by which companies are directed and controlled, promoting accountability.
items.domain_ref: Business organisational structure, functions and governance
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A manager uses a style where decisions are made jointly with the team and members are consulted. Which leadership style is this?

options.rationale: Correct: consulting and deciding jointly with the team describes a democratic/participative style.
An autocratic leader decides alone without consulting the team.
A laissez-faire leader leaves the team to make its own decisions with little input.
A bureaucratic style relies on strict rules and procedures, not joint decisions.

items.explanation: Correct: consulting and deciding jointly with the team describes a democratic/participative style.
items.domain_ref: Leading and managing individuals and teams

items.stem: Select TWO fundamental principles of the professional accountant's code of ethics.

options.rationale: Correct: integrity is a fundamental ethical principle.
Correct: objectivity is a fundamental ethical principle.
Profit maximisation is not an ethical principle in the code.
Growing market share is a business goal, not an ethical principle.
Confidentiality is bounded by law; concealment from regulators is not a principle.

items.explanation: Correct: integrity is a fundamental ethical principle.
